newsitem.title: UK: France wants to probe Eurotunnel "insider dealing'.
newsitem.headline: France wants to probe Eurotunnel "insider dealing'.

text.p: French police want to raid some of Britain's leading banks and financial institutions to probe allegations of insider dealing in the shares of debt-laden Channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel, the Sunday Times said.

The newspaper said French fraud squad detectives visited Britain's Serious Fraud Office (SFO) last week to ask for help in an investigation into claims that details of Eurotunnel's financial restructuring had been leaked.
An SFO spokesman declined to comment on the story.

The paper said the deals in question stretched back to 1994, the year the tunnel opened, and were understood to have taken place before the Anglo-French consortium made announcements about efforts to reschedule its debts.
Earlier this year former Eurotunnel co-chairman Sir Alistair Morton accused some dealers of deliberately driving down the consortium's share price.
Last month Eurotunnel worked out a complex deal with its major creditors to reschedule its 9.1 billion pounds ($14.5 billion) of debt.
